title: A core's own Part History page shows its name and its history
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919); the Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Part Library & Inventory → Create & Edit' and 'Part Library & Inventory → Delete' and can see costs and prices.
  • Bin {Bin-A} is the default bin of {Location-A} (for example General Storage), the bin New Inventory Part fills in.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-CORE-HIST-01) is active and tracked at {Location-A}, with 2 in {Bin-A} and a Core Charge of $25.00, so it has a core, {Core-A}.
  • {Part-A}'s description was changed in its Edit Inventory Part dialog from {Description-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL CORE HISTORY OLD) to {Description-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST PL CORE HISTORY NEW) after the core existed.
  • The way to open {Core-A}'s own Part History page was found and written down during setup.
custom_steps:
1. Open {Core-A}'s Part History page the way written down during setup.
  2. Read the name at the top of the Part details panel.
  3. Read the newest entry in the Part History table.
  4. Go to Parts → Inventory, search the part number of {Part-A} and click the clock icon (tooltip "Part History") on its row.
  5. Read the newest entry in that Part History table.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: A Part History page opens for the core, not for {Part-A}.
  • Step 2: The Part details panel names the core "Core for {Description-B}" (a long name may be cut short with two dots): the core was renamed with its part.
  • Step 3: The newest entry reads "Description updated | Original description: Core for {Description-A} | New description: Core for {Description-B}", with your name under Staff and today's date and time.
  • Step 5: {Part-A}'s own newest entry reads "Description updated | Original description: {Description-A} | New description: {Description-B}": the core keeps a history of its own.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10818 (Story 5, Change Tracking on an Existing Part); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S5-E3, with the core's name from S13-R15 and the entry texts from S10-R24 and S10-R26, read 14 Oct 2026; Product's answer of 13 Oct (Chris Ward, question 6: "Its name and history show on the core's own Part History page."). Design: no board shows a core; Part History layout from board 2.4 (Part History at Heavy Duty), 13 Oct copy, unchanged on 14 Oct. No source names the link that opens a core's Part History page (question in the notes). Story SV-10818 (updated 9 Oct 2026) does not yet carry S5-E3; the PRD wins. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-E3: “A core has no row of its own on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list, so it cannot be ticked for a bulk change. Its name (S13-R15) and its history show on the core's own Part History page. The core reason in S10-R13a applies when a core reaches a status change by any other route.”
  • S13-R15: “A changed description also renames the part's core, which reads "Core for {description}".”
  • S10-R26: “When the part has a core, the core gets the same number or description entry. The core's description entries read its own description, "Core for {description}".”
  • S10-R24: “A changed description writes "Description updated | Original description: {old} | New description: {new}" to the Part History of the part at every location that stocks it.”
